"History of Liberia

Liberia is a country in West Africa which was founded, established, colonized, and controlled by citizens of the United States and ex-Caribbean slaves as a colony for former African American slaves and their free black descendants. It is one of only two sovereign countries in the world that were started ... the other being Sierra Leone, established by Great Britain. In 1847, Liberia proclaimed its independence from the American Colonization Society (ACS)."

We need triplets.

Entities: Liberia (country), West Africa (region), United States (country), ex-Caribbean slaves (group), African American slaves (group), free black descendants (group), Sierra Leone (country), Great Britain (country), 1847 (date), American Colonization Society (organisation), independence (event), colonized, founded, established, controlled.

We need to capture:

- Liberia is a country. relation: "instance of" maybe but typical relation "country" maybe "subclass of"? In examples they used "occupation", "award". For location: "country" maybe "instance of" with object "country". But we can use relation "instance of" with object "country". subject_type "sovereign state". object_type "country". Let's follow pattern: "Liberia", "instance of", "country". qualifiers none.

- Liberia located in West Africa. relation "located in". object "West Africa". subject_type "country", object_type "region".

- Liberia was founded by citizens of the United States and ex-Caribbean slaves. This is a complex: "founder" relation? Could have two separate triplets: founder: United States (citizens) and ex-Caribbean slaves (group). But "citizens of the United States" is a group; we can treat subject "Liberia", relation "founded by", object "citizens of the United States". Also separate "founded by" ex-Caribbean slaves. Also "established by" same? The text says "founded, established, colonized, and controlled by". Could create multiple relations: "founded by", "established by", "colonized by", "controlled by". Might be redundant but okay.

- Also "as a colony for former African American slaves and their free black descendants." So relation "purpose" maybe "colony for". Could use relation "intended for" or "purpose". Let's use "purpose" with object "former African American slaves and their free black descendants". Could also split into two: "purpose" "former African American slaves", and "purpose" "free black descendants". But maybe combine.

- "It is one of only two sovereign countries in the world that were started by citizens and ex-Caribbean slaves of a political power as a colony for former slaves of the same political power, the other being Sierra Leone, established by Great Britain." So we need triplet: "Sierra Leone", "instance of", "sovereign country". Also "Sierra Leone", "established by", "Great Britain". Also maybe "Liberia" "one of only two sovereign countries ...". That's a statement, but maybe not needed.

- "In 1847, Liberia proclaimed its independence from the American Colonization Society (ACS)." So event: "Liberia", "proclaimed independence", object "American Colonization Society". With qualifier point in time 1847. Also maybe relation "independence from" but we can use "independence declared from". Let's use relation "proclaimed independence". object "American Colonization Society". qualifiers point in time 1847.

- Also "American Colonization Society" type organization.

- Also "Great Britain" type country.

- "citizens of the United States" type group? Could be "citizens of United States". We'll set object_type "group of people". Similarly "ex-Caribbean slaves" group.

- "former African American slaves" group.
